changes: No substantive changes. Checked the date: ŚS 1791 (+78) and VS 1926 (−57) agree, and since Māgha śukla falls in January or February, the CE date is early 1870. The note now gives this reasoning.

purpose: dedication: śrīvāsayaṇārpaṇam astu (probably for śrīnārāyaṇārpaṇam astu)
notes: The colophon gives the date in two eras, and they agree: ŚS 1791 and VS 1926 both correspond to 1869/70 CE. Māgha śukla 8 falls in January or February 1870. 'śrīvāsayaṇārpaṇam astu' is probably a corruption of śrīnārāyaṇārpaṇam astu, though śrīvāsudevārpaṇam is also possible. The Nīlakaṇṭha named here is the author of the text, not someone connected with this copy.
